text: Fill in the key term for each statement about bone.
questions: The organic part of bone matrix is mainly type I *collagen:Which fibrous protein resists stretching?*, which gives toughness.
The inorganic part is calcium phosphate laid down as crystals of *hydroxyapatite/hydroxy apatite/hydroxy-apatite:Name the mineral crystal form in bone.*.
Osteoblasts lay down new bone matrix, while *osteoclasts:Which cells break down bone?* resorb bone.
Osteocytes occupy small spaces in the matrix called *lacunae:What is the Latin term for these tiny chambers?*.

overallFeedback.feedback: Bone's two-phase matrix combines collagen (about one-third of dry weight, providing toughness by resisting tension) and hydroxyapatite crystals (about two-thirds, providing hardness by resisting compression). Osteoclasts, derived from the monocyte–macrophage line, resorb bone during remodelling, while osteocytes maintain the matrix from within their lacunae, connected by fine canaliculi.
